newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends down after dlr short covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends down after dlr short covering.

text.p: The won ended Thursday's session slightly lower after recouping from a morning of agressive dollar short covering, traders said.

The won finished at 888.10 against Wednesday's close of 888.00. After opening at a high of 887.90, the won fell to 888.90 during the morning session as the central bank's intervention on Wednesday forced shorts to cover their dollar positions.
But they said the won recovered in afternoon trading ahead of month-end export negotiations and incoming foreign funds for equity investments.
"There will be a growing demand for the won as we approach the end of the month, so I expect the won to rise to 887.20/30 tomorrow," said a local bank dealer.
He added another central bank intervention could be expected if the won strengthens further.
Friday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 888.30 from 887.70 today.
